# Private credit marks climb toward public strength

**Rating: overweight**

The gap between reported and public performance—reported_vs_public_gap at -8.5%—reads to us as lag, not deception. Public rally leaves private marks behind precisely because private valuations move on a quarterly cadence while listed comps rerate sharply in real time. With drawdown at +0.0% and a one_year_return of +9.3%, the underlying book has not cracked; it has simply not yet been asked to catch up to the marks the public market is already pricing. We expect that catch-up to arrive as valuation cycles turn, not as a shock.

Grimshaw Partners frames this same gap as fragility compounding beneath stable marks. We read the identical spread differently: hy_spread_now_bps at 380bps remains consistent with a credit complex under manageable stress, not one masking hidden deterioration. Policy_rate_now at 4.75% against cpi_now of 2.7% still leaves real rates restrictive enough to reward patient capital, and as the policy stance eases over time—our house view holds that growth and policy support resolve stress rather than entrench it—the private-public gap should compress from the private side up, not the public side down.

Ytd_return of +1.0% looks thin in isolation, but set against a full one_year_return of +9.3% it reads as a pause within an otherwise constructive trend, consistent with marks digesting the public rerating before following it upward.

The risk to this view: if reported marks are understating stress rather than merely lagging it, the -8.5% gap could widen instead of close, and a compression trade built on convergence would be premature. We think this risk is manageable but watch it closely, and would treat any evidence of marks moving away from—rather than toward—public levels as reason to reconsider the overweight.
